label: caiso 172 measured path15
definition: KEEPER (caiso-172, 2026-08-04). The MEASURED Path-15 split of PG&E TAC load: CAISO_TAC_ZONE_WEIGHTS['PGE-TAC'] moves from the 0.86/0.14 estimate of 'unverified provenance' — the LAST residual-identified member of that table (audit C-16, issue #1372) — to 0.883951/0.116049, derived by scripts/data/derive_caiso_path15_load_split.py from two PUBLISHED CAISO OASIS Atlas reports: ATL_LDF's per-pnode load distribution factors inside DLAP_PGAE-APND joined by substation to ATL_PNODE_MAP's authoritative TH_NP15_GEN / TH_ZP26_GEN membership (CAISO's own Path-15 geography). The estimate put 17% too much PG&E load in ZP26. ZERO free parameters and ZERO ScenarioConfig fields — a rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] measured-over-estimate substitution and a rule 20 [R-DOF] CLOSURE: n_residual 9 -> 8, CAISO's ISO-specific residual count 4 -> 3. Determination-NEUTRAL against its own same-head control (CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, 0 FAILs, same 2 ledgered caveats, same C3a +11.5%/+14.4%), so it costs nothing and buys a DOF. Quantity effect measured, not asserted: ZP26 served energy -17.11% and NP15 +2.79% in every year at ISO total unchanged; Path-15 N->S flow -13.2/-12.2/-12.0% (10.27->8.92, 12.19->10.70, 12.23->10.77 TWh). The NP15-ZP26 basis moves TOWARD the measured +5.947/+8.576/+5.727 $/MWh (+0.236->+0.333, +0.127->+0.217, +0.109->+0.179, i.e. 4.0->5.6%, 1.5->2.5%, 1.9->3.1% of measured) but KNOWN-OPEN 1 stays wide open and this was pre-registered as REPORTED, NOT GATED.
market_story: This run changes WHERE PG&E's load sits, not how any plant offers. PG&E's TAC area straddles Path 15, and the model had been putting 14% of it in ZP26 — the San Joaquin Valley between Path 15 and Path 26 — on a ratio nobody could source. CAISO's own published load distribution factors say 11.6%. The real market puts less load south of Path 15 than the model assumed, because the PG&E sub-LAPs that actually sit there (SLAP_PGZP and Kern) are agricultural and oil-field load, while the Bay Area, Sacramento Valley, Fresno and the Central Coast — the bulk of PG&E's customers — are north of the boundary. Moving 2.1-2.3 TWh/yr of demand from ZP26 to NP15 does exactly what physics says it should: the Path-15 north-to-south transfer that used to serve that load falls by ~1.4 TWh/yr and the link sits at its bound in fewer hours (2025: 21 -> 13). Prices barely move because neither zone was scarce at the margin — which is the honest result, and the reason this is filed as an input correction rather than a lever: it makes the load allocation true, and it does not pretend to close the north-south congestion basis, which remains 3-6% represented.
